==English==
''[[Wiktionary:Word of the day/Archive/2015/August#9|WOTD – 9 August 2015]][[Category:Word of the day archive/2015/August]][[Category:Word of the day archive/2015]][[Category:Word of the day archive]]''
===Pronunciation=== * [[Wiktionary:International Phonetic Alphabet|IPA]]([[Appendix:English pronunciation|key]]): /lɑː/[[Category:English 1-syllable words|LAH]][[Category:English terms with IPA pronunciation|LAH]] **
Audio ([[w:English in southern England|Southern England]]):[[File:LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-lah.wav|noicon|175px]]([[:File:LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-lah.wav|file]])
[[Category:English terms with audio pronunciation|LAH]] * Rhymes: [[Rhymes:English/ɑː|-ɑː]][[Category:Rhymes:English/ɑː|LAH]][[Category:Rhymes:English/ɑː/1 syllable|LAH]] ===Etymology 1===
    An anglicised spelling of [[:la#English|la]]. ====Noun==== lah (plural [[:lahs#English|lahs]])[[Category:English lemmas|LAH]][[Category:English nouns|LAH]][[Category:English countable nouns|LAH]][[Category:English entries with incorrect language header|LAH]][[Category:Pages with entries|LAH]][[Category:Pages with 9 entries|LAH]] # ([[music|music]][[Category:en:Music|LAH]]) Alternative spelling of [[:la#English|la]]. ===Etymology 2===
      [[File:Wikipedia-logo-v2.svg|x40px|none|link=|alt=]]
      English [[Wikipedia]] has an article on:
      [[:w:Singlish#Lah|Singlish]][[Category:English links with redundant alt parameters|LAH]]
      [[w:Singlish#Lah|Wikipedia ]]
      [[File:Wikipedia-logo-v2.svg|x40px|none|link=|alt=]]
      English [[Wikipedia]] has an article on:
      [[:w:Manglish#Lah|Manglish]][[Category:English links with redundant alt parameters|LAH]]
      [[w:Manglish#Lah|Wikipedia ]]
      From [[w:Malay language|Malay]][[Category:English terms derived from Malay|LAH]] [[:lah#Malay|lah]], [[w:Hokkien|Hokkien]][[Category:English terms derived from Hokkien|LAH]] [[啦#Chinese|啦]] (--la) and [[w:Cantonese|Cantonese]][[Category:English terms derived from Cantonese|LAH]] [[啦#Chinese|啦]] (laa1). [[Appendix:Glossary#doublet|Doublet]] of [[:la#Etymology 6|la]][[Category:English links with manual fragments|LAH]][[Category:English doublets|LAH]] in colloquial [[w:Hong Kong English|Hong Kong English]]. Lim (2007) lists multiple sources: * [[w:Malay trade and creole languages#Singapore Bazaar Malay|Bazaar Malay]], for its use as a particle of emphasis (akin to [[w:Malay language|Malay]] [[:lah#Malay|lah]]), and the senses expressing commands, invitations and "solidarity, familiarity [and] informality". * [[w:Hokkien|Hokkien]][[Category:English terms derived from Hokkien|LAH]] [[啦#Chinese|啦]] (--la), which indicates finality, completion and confirmation-seeking, as well as "emphasis, persuasiveness, dismissiveness [and] listing". * [[w:Cantonese|Cantonese]][[Category:English terms derived from Cantonese|LAH]] [[啦#Chinese|啦]] (laa1), expressing a "general lack of definiteness or forcefulness", and for its role in softening commands. ====Alternative forms==== * [[:la#English|la]], [[:lar#English|lar]] ====Pronunciation==== * ([[w:Singapore English|Singapore]], [[w:Malaysian English|Malaysia]]) [[Wiktionary:International Phonetic Alphabet|IPA]]([[Appendix:English pronunciation|key]]): /lɑː/, [lä(ː)][[Category:English 1-syllable words|LAH]][[Category:English terms with IPA pronunciation|LAH]]* ** *The different senses of this word are distinguished by lexical tone. ** Variant for senses 1–4: [[Wiktionary:International Phonetic Alphabet|IPA]]([[Appendix:English pronunciation|key]]): [lɑh˨][[Category:English terms with IPA pronunciation|LAH]] ====Particle==== lah[[Category:English lemmas|LAH]][[Category:English particles|LAH]][[Category:English entries with incorrect language header|LAH]][[Category:Pages with entries|LAH]][[Category:Pages with 9 entries|LAH]] ([[w:Manglish|Manglish]][[Category:Manglish|LAH]], [[w:Singlish|Singlish]][[Category:Singlish|LAH]], clause-final [[w:Discourse marker|discourse particle]]) #
    • Placed at the end of a sentence to accentuate the [[:mood#English|mood]] or [[:attitude#English|attitude]] of the speaker. [from mid-20th c.] #: Pitch contour: low-mid [lɑ(ː)˨], mid-falling [lɑː˧˨] #: Don’t do it '''lah''', it’s not worth it. ― ''Disapproval''[[Category:English terms with usage examples|LAH]] #: Hurry up, '''lah'''! ― ''Impatience''[[Category:English terms with usage examples|LAH]] #*
      '''1978''', ''Leong'' Choon Cheong, Youth in the Army, Singapore: Federal Publications, [https://search.worldcat.org/title/6144357 →OCLC], page 75:[[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      Don’t know '''lah''' […] this is very hard to say.
      [[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      #*
      '''2007''', Elangovan, P, Singapore, [[Special:BookSources/9789810589509|→ISBN]], [https://search.worldcat.org/title/1050752756 →OCLC], page 47:[[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      Even if you don't know, just pretend as if you know-'''lah''' Mike. You are embarrassing me you know.
      [[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      #*
      '''2020''', Stephanie Street, Dragonflies, Epigram Books, [[Special:BookSources/9789814845960|→ISBN]], Act 2, scene 2, page 110:[[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      Please '''lah''', you want to save me, save me the headache.
      [[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      #*
      '''2024''' July 16, Clement Yong, “Theatre review: National Day Charade mimes familiar criticisms of NDP but doles out a lesson or two”, in [[:w:The Straits Times|The Straits Times]], Singapore: Singapore Press Holdings Limited:[[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      In a few months that have been both dispiriting and heartening with regard to public art […] is it any wonder that one of the most earnest things one can say to Singapore right now is: “Stop complaining, '''lah'''”?
      [[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      #* For more quotations using this term, see [[Citations:lah#English|Citations:lah]]. #
    • Placed at the end of a sentence to convey [[:reassurance#English|reassurance]] or express [[:solidarity#English|solidarity]]. #: Pitch contour: low-mid [lɑ(ː)˨], mid-falling [lɑː˧˨] #:
      You won’t drown [[:one#Particle|one]] '''lah'''. The water is very shallow.
      [[Category:English terms with usage examples|LAH]] #*
      '''1999''', [[:w:Alfian Sa'at|Alfian Sa'at]], [[:w:Corridor (short story collection)|Corridor]], Singapore: SNP Editions, [https://search.worldcat.org/title/42753130 →OCLC], page 15:[[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      Don’t worry '''lah'''. We’ll meet the deadline.
      [[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      #
    • Indicates an attempt at expressing [[:sympathy#English|sympathy]], conveying [[:informality#English|informality]] or [[:sincerity#English|sincerity]], or establishing a [[:rapport#English|rapport]] with the listener. #: Pitch contour: low-mid [lɑ(ː)˨] #:
      Just try your best '''lah''', and don’t think too much about it.
      [[Category:English terms with usage examples|LAH]] #*
      '''1990''', [[:w:Kuo Pao Kun|Pao Kun Kuo]], “No Parking On Odd Days”, in The Coffin Is Too Big For The Hole and Other Plays, [https://search.worldcat.org/title/1391287329 →OCLC], page 63:[[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      I mean, I didn’t want to break the law, and I honestly went down to find out whether that place was OK to park [[:or not#Particle|or not]]. Let’s be fair '''lah''', you can’t expect me to see one sign saying something and still go a long way to see if there is another one saying something else.
      [[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      #*
      '''2016''', Junjia Ye, quoting Jayakumar, chapter 5, in Class Inequality in the Global City: Migrants, Workers and Cosmopolitanism in Singapore, Palgrave Macmillan UK, [[Special:BookSources/9781137436153|→ISBN]], pages 139–140:[[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      I had Malay friends who were just turned away like that. It’s quite bad '''''lah'''''.
      [[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      #*
      '''2022''', Hunter Ng, As Coarse as Emporium, Jettison Books, [[Special:BookSources/9789811840098|→ISBN]]:[[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      You know that for tattooing, we are supposed to use disposable needles, right? Well, Joseph (Rough Face) will tell us not to throw them away after use. The next morning when I come into the studio, the needle box is always full again but the needles are without their original seal. You know why '''lah'''.
      [[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      #*
      '''2024''', Jojo Chia, Afternoon Yuan Yang Club, Epigram Books, [[Special:BookSources/9789815105797|→ISBN]]:[[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      [[:aiya#English|Aiyah]], we will always chat or message [[:what#Particle|what]]... We’ll keep in touch '''lah''', [[:hor#Etymology 2|hor]]?
      [[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      #
    • Placed at the end of an assertive statement to express [[:denial#English|denial]] or [[:dismissiveness#English|dismissiveness]]. #: Pitch contour: low-mid [lɑ(ː)˨], mid-falling [lɑː˧˨] #:
      — I don’t think you should be cutting corners, at least put in some effort and make it look legit.
      — They won’t care [[:one#Etymology 2|one]] '''lah'''... I don’t have all day...
      [[Category:English terms with usage examples|LAH]] #*
      '''2011''', [[:w:Robert Yeo|Robert Yeo]], The Adventures of Holden Heng, Epigram Books, [[Special:BookSources/9789810762513|→ISBN]]:[[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      “No '''lah''',” she had said, almost casually to his proposal. He was flabbergasted.
      [[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      #*
      '''2011''', Siong Chye Sim, Once Bitten, Never Shy: Confessions of a Backpacking Diplomat, Armour, [[Special:BookSources/9789814305396|→ISBN]], page 63:[[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      Don’t bother about him '''lah'''. Let’s pack up and get some sleep as we have a long day ahead.
      [[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      #*
      '''2012''' March 25, Maureen Koh, quoting Ha Wai Kay, “Her luck is in the duck”, in [[:w:The Straits Times|The Straits Times]], Singapore: Singapore Press Holdings Limited, PEOPLE, pages 6–7:[[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      No '''lah''', they must look at it this way... even though the founder (Colonel Harland Sanders) of KFC has died, his recipe lives on.
      [[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      #*
      '''2013''', [[:w:Kevin Kwan|Kevin Kwan]], chapter 3, in Crazy Rich Asians, [[:w:Doubleday (publisher)|Doubleday]], [[Special:BookSources/9780385536981|→ISBN]]:[[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      “Papa, I’m telling you—the property was immense. It was like the [[:w:The Istana|''Istana'']]. The driveway itself went on for miles.”
      “Cannot be! Two or three acres I might believe, but fifty? No such thing, '''''lah'''''.”
      [[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      #
    • Used after an [[:assertive#English|assertive]] statement to reinforce its [[:authoritativeness#English|authoritativeness]], or to show that the speaker is [[:confident#English|confident]] with what they are saying. #: Pitch contour: low-mid [lɑ(ː)˨], mid-falling [lɑː˧˨] #:
      These shoes are too small '''lah'''.
      [[Category:English terms with usage examples|LAH]] #:
      No need to count '''lah'''. I’m sure the number is right.
      [[Category:English terms with usage examples|LAH]] #*
      '''1997''', [[:w:Eric Khoo|Eric Khoo]], James Toh, 00:27:01 from the start, in [[:w:12 Storeys|12 Storeys]]:[[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      Eleven, eleven thirty, [[:same same#English|same same]] '''lah'''.
      [[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      #*
      '''2007''', [[:w:Michael Vatikiotis|Michael Vatikiotis]], Singapore Ground Zero, Talisman, [[Special:BookSources/9789810587826|→ISBN]], page 3:[[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      Every once in a long while when someone asked why, he said: “No time-'''lah'''. So busy-[[:leh#English:_remark|leh]].”
      [[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      #*
      '''2008''', [[:w:Preeta Samarasan|Preeta Samarasan]], Evening Is the Whole Day, Fourth Estate, [[Special:BookSources/9780007271887|→ISBN]], [https://search.worldcat.org/title/1244716239 →OCLC], page 116:[[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      “Keretapi Tanah Melayu means railway '''lah''' thanggachi [[[:தங்கச்சி#Tamil|தங்கச்சி]] (taṅkacci)[[Category:Tamil terms with non-redundant manual transliterations|LAH]], term of address for a younger woman],” the man went on. “Means Malay Land Railway. Malay Land that means Malaysia [[:lah#English:_clear|lah]] [Sense 6], thanggachi, that also you don’t know [[:ah#Etymology 2|ah]]? […]
      [[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      #
    • Asserts that something is clear, obvious or [[:straightforward#English|straightforward]]. #: Pitch contour: falling [lɑ(ː)˦˨] #: Near-synonym: [[:lor#English:_obvious-answer|lor]] (sense 2) #:
      Get a whiteboard marker and write over it '''lah'''.
      [[Category:English terms with usage examples|LAH]] #:
      They’re not wrong '''lah'''... But they’re only taking themselves into consideration.
      [[Category:English terms with usage examples|LAH]] #*
      '''2009''', [[:w:Jean Tay|Jean Tay]], Boom, Epigram Books, [[Special:BookSources/9810755007|→ISBN]], Act I, scene v, page 30:[[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      Mud you can clean up. Cobwebs you can sweep away. Stains, use bleach '''lah'''!
      [[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      #*
      '''2009''', [[:w:Alfian Sa'at|Alfian Sa'at]], “Nadirah”, in Collected Plays Three, Singapore, [[Special:BookSources/9789811400421|→ISBN]], Scene ii, page 57:[[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      Nadirah: You never told me Sally was leaving. I didn't even have the chance to say goodbye.
      Sahirah: You visit her '''lah''' when you go to KL.
      [[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      #
    • Used to [[:tone down#English|tone down]] an [[:imperative#English|imperative]] sentence, so it sounds more like a [[:request#English|request]] or [[:suggestion#English|suggestion]]. #: Pitch contour: falling [lɑ(ː)˦˨] #*
      '''2013''' June 18, Huang Lijie, quoting Samantha Lo, “Sticking to budding artist label”, in [[:w:The Straits Times|The Straits Times]], Singapore: Singapore Press Holdings Limited, LIFE! Arts, page 2:[[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      I remember my friends telling me, 'People already say you're an artist, then be one '''lah'''.'
      [[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      #
    • Indicates strong [[:persuasion#English|persuasion]] at the end of an imperative sentence. #: Pitch contour: mid-falling [lɑː˧˨] #:
      Don’t waste your time there '''lah'''.
      [[Category:English terms with usage examples|LAH]] #*
      '''2014''', Danielle Lim, The Sound of SCH: A Mental Breakdown, A Life Journey, Ethos Books, [[Special:BookSources/9789811176043|→ISBN]]:[[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      […] I say politely, No thank you, it’s okay. But he insists, Take '''lah''', never mind, no need to [[:paiseh#English|''pai-seh'']]!
      [[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      #
    • Indicates a [[:retrospective#English|retrospective]] [[:remark#English|remark]] or a [[:reassessment#English|reassessment]] of one’s opinion. #: Pitch contour: low-mid [lɑ(ː)˨], mid-falling [lɑː˧˨] #:
      — Not many people would think of using a pressure cooker.
      — I mean, it’s pretty unconventional '''lah''', I have to admit.
      [[Category:English terms with usage examples|LAH]] #*
      '''1994''', C. S. Chong, NS: An Air-Level Story, Singapore: Times Books International, [[Special:BookSources/978-981-204-312-2|→ISBN]], page 58:[[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      Oh well, it was [[:siong#English|xiong]], but overall OK, '''lah'''.
      [[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      #*
      '''2019''' March 5, [[:w:Ong Ye Kung|Ong Ye Kung]], “Committee of Supply – Head K (Ministry of Education)”, in Parliamentary Debates: Official Report (Parliament of Singapore), volume 94:[[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      He said that in the past, […] a teacher might admonish a noisy class and say: “4N(T), keep quiet!” Immediately, all the N(T) students felt that they were singled out. Today, the teacher would say: “NCC, keep quiet!” and the Normal stream students feel: “Okay '''lah'''.”
      [[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      #*
      '''2021''' December 9, Ilyas Sholihyn, Rainer Cheung, quoting Syed, “20 Years On, What Do Singaporeans Remember About JI’s Failed Bomb Plot?”, in ricemedia.co‎[https://web.archive.org/web/20241209190011/https://www.ricemedia.co/feature-singaporeans-remember-jemaah-islamiyah-ji/], archived from [https://www.ricemedia.co/feature-singaporeans-remember-jemaah-islamiyah-ji/ the original] on 9 December 2024:[[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      Different priorities '''lah''' these days.
      [[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      #*
      '''2022''', Bernice Loh, chapter 4, in Tween Girls' Dressing and Young Femininity in Singapore: Too Much, Too Young, Too Fast?, Springer Nature Singapore, [[Special:BookSources/9789811695117|→ISBN]], page 94:[[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      Interviewer: But what is expensive to your parents? Like $50 for a dress?
      Lola: Er ... it’s not that bad '''lah'''.
      [[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      #
    • Reinforces a [[:suggestion#English|suggestion]] with the implication that it is the more [[:practical#English|practical]] option. #: Pitch contour: low-mid [lɑ(ː)˨], mid-falling [lɑː˧˨] #:
      The nearest train station is 15 minutes away. I think we take the bus '''lah''', [[:hor#English|hor]]?
      [[Category:English terms with usage examples|LAH]] #:
      Use the mittens '''lah'''.
      [[Category:English terms with usage examples|LAH]] #
    • Indicates [[:confirmation#English|confirmation]]-seeking at the end of an [[:inferential#English|inferential]] statement. #: Pitch contour: falling [lɑː˦˨] #:
      In other words, you’re the one who started it '''lah'''!
      [[Category:English terms with usage examples|LAH]] #*
      '''2019''' June 4, Ethel Pang, “As Long As SAP Schools Exist, ‘Chinese Elitism’ in Singapore Will Exist”, in ricemedia.co‎[https://web.archive.org/web/20250210090622/https://www.ricemedia.co/current-affairs-opinion-sap-schools-chinese-elitism-singapore/], archived from [https://www.ricemedia.co/current-affairs-opinion-sap-schools-chinese-elitism-singapore/ the original] on 10 February 2025:[[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      “Huh? [[:w:Special Assistance Plan|SAP]] school? Oh, you mean Chinese schools '''lah'''.”
      [[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      #
    • Used to express [[:realisation#English|realisation]], or [[:vexation#English|vexation]] when something is already obvious. #: Pitch contour: falling [lɑː˦˨] #:
      So in the end it wasn’t my fault '''lah'''!
      [[Category:English terms with usage examples|LAH]] #:
      Do it yourself '''lah'''! Always need me to help [[:is it#English|is it]]?
      [[Category:English terms with usage examples|LAH]] #*
      '''1983''', Stella Kon, [[:w:Emily of Emerald Hill|Emily of Emerald Hill]], [[Special:BookSources/9789811118562|→ISBN]], Act 1, page 14:[[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      When Richard was going to join Anglo-Chinese School I expected the father to bring him to see the Headmaster, after all he was from ACS himself, but he couldn't be bothered. (''Emily imitates Kheong's brusque brush-off'') 'You look after it, you arrange it '''lah'''!'
      [[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      #
    • (less common) Reinforces the factuality of an assertive statement made to correct an inaccurate, underlying [[:assumption#English|assumption]]. #: Pitch contour: mid-rising [lɑ(ː)˧˦] #:
      Oh wait it’s not today, '''lah'''. It’s on Sunday.
      [[Category:English terms with usage examples|LAH]] #
    • (less common) Used to convey a slight sense of [[:dissatisfaction#English|dissatisfaction]] or [[:irritation#English|irritation]]. #: Pitch contour: mid-rising [lɑ(ː)˧˦] #
    • (less common) Used for [[:enumeration#English|enumeration]] (when listing [[:example#English|example]]s). #: Pitch contour: mid [lɑː˧] #*
      '''2010''', [[:w:Haresh Sharma|Haresh Sharma]], Those Who Can't, Teach, Epigram Books, Act I, scene ii:[[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      He teach them how to cook '''lah''', learn computer '''lah'''... […]
      [[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      #*
      '''2011''', Prem Anand, J T Koh, S. Rajaretnam, [[:w:The Noose (TV series)|The Noose]], season 4, episode 10 (television production), spoken by Pak Samad (Nasi Lemak Store Owner) ([[:w:Suhaimi Yusof|Suhaimi Yusof]]), via [[:w:Channel 5 (Singaporean TV channel)|Channel 5 (Mediacorp)]]:[[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      Nasi lemak, is nasi lemak [[:lah#English:_authoritativeness|lah]] [sense 6]. It's not like you have to put in all this extra thing like what, foie gras '''lah'''...
      [[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]

    • (chiefly [[w:Malaysian English|Malaysia]][[Category:Malaysian English|LAH]], less common in [[w:Singapore English|Singapore]][[Category:Singapore English|LAH]]) An [[:assertive#English|assertive]] separator, used to reverse the order of the usual [[:w:Topic and comment|topic–comment structure]] of a sentence. #: Pitch contour: low-mid [lɑ(ː)˨] #: No fun '''lah''', you. ― You’re no fun.[[Category:English terms with usage examples|LAH]] #*
      '''2014''', Latha [K. Kanagalatha], The Goddesses in the Living Room, Singapore: Epigram Books, [[Special:BookSources/9814615153|→ISBN]], page 102:[[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      “Who '''lah''' that [[:w:Draupadi|Panjali]]? A real ‘number nine’ [From [[:w:Tamil language|Tamil]] [[:ஒன்பது#Tamil|ஒன்பது]] (oṉpatu), a derogatory term for a transgender person].”
      “You don’t play a fool you know. He is not a ‘number nine’, not a hermaphrodite, but a man. He is the one who has been cross-dressing and performing the role of Panjali for many years.”
      [[Category:English terms with quotations|LAH]]
      #
    • (less common) Used [[:sarcastically#English|sarcastically]]. #: Pitch contour: low-mid [lɑː˨], (''in the example below'') high-mid [lɑ(ː)˦] #: No '''lah''', no '''lah'''. ― No, definitely not. (''sarcastic reply'')[[Category:English terms with usage examples|LAH]] =====Usage notes===== As demonstrated by German & Prevot (2014), ''lah'' is more likely to occur after clauses ending in a lexically stressed syllable (e.g., ''No need, lah!'') than after clauses ending in an unstressed syllable, generally speaking.
